evals.prompt: On paper, review a native Zsh 5.9 sourced plugin that sets KSH_ARRAYS and SH_WORD_SPLIT globally, overwrites precmd and calls compinit -u. Can ShellCheck --shell=bash validate it? Do not run or change anything.
evals.expected_output: Preserves native semantics and caller ownership while using the native Zsh verification lane.
expectations: Explains native one-based arrays and nonsplitting scalar expansion together with the named option effects.
Rejects Bash-mode ShellCheck as native Zsh validation.
Does not reset a completion function option environment blindly with emulate -L zsh.
Protects existing hooks and preserves compaudit checks instead of recommending compinit -u.
Requires explicit ownership or restoration of changed caller options and registrations.

evals.prompt: Our native Zsh targets 5.9, 5.9.1 and 5.9.2. A source says real-time signals, kill -q/-L and _as_if arrived in 5.9.2. Check that claim and plan optional-module and new-syntax gates. Do not execute commands.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the feature attribution and distinguishes version gates, parse-time isolation and build capabilities.
expectations: Attributes the listed signal and completion additions to Zsh 5.9.1 using the official release notes.
Does not claim that the upstream 5.9.2 test result proves 5.9 or macOS compatibility.
Uses a numeric-aware version mechanism such as is-at-least rather than lexical comparison.
Separates optional module availability from the language version.
Keeps newer parse-time syntax in a separately selected file rather than assuming an if branch hides it.

evals.prompt: Review a proposed read-only check: zsh -f -n plugin.zsh, then automatically run plugin.zsh with a temporary ZDOTDIR. The plugin includes a ZLE widget and autoloaded function. Explain the evidence and startup boundary only; run no commands.
evals.expected_output: Keeps syntax, smoke, semantic and PTY evidence separate and requires explicit execution scope.
expectations: States that -n parses without executing the target body and does not test its behavior.
States that global zshenv can still run under -f and a temporary ZDOTDIR is not containment.
Does not automatically execute the plugin after a syntax-only request.
Requires role-specific autoload and PTY tests for the function and ZLE widget.
Does not claim that top-level emulate -L zsh localizes state as it does inside an enclosing function.
